group.passage:
Every ten years, the United States must count all of its people, because the result decides how many seats each state receives in Congress. By the 1880s, this duty had turned into a race the government was losing. Even with the help of simple tally machines, clerks did not finish adding up the 1880 figures until 1887, about seven years after the count began. As the population kept growing, experts warned that the 1890 census might take 13 years to process, so its results would not be ready before the next count in 1900.
Herman Hollerith, a young engineer who had worked on the 1880 census, believed a machine could do the job. Part of his inspiration came from watching a train conductor punch holes in passengers' tickets. He first tried long rolls of paper but switched to cards, which lasted longer and were easier to feed through a machine. In his system, every person became one paper card, and a hole in a particular position stood for a single fact, such as male, female, or a certain age. When a clerk pressed a card into the reader, metal pins passed through the holes and dipped into small cups of mercury. Each pin that got through completed an electric circuit, which moved the matching dial forward by one.
In 1888, the census office held a contest using old figures from four areas of St. Louis. The two rival methods needed 44.5 and 55.5 hours to prepare the data for counting, while Hollerith's needed only 5.5. He won the contract, and with clerks punching some 500 cards a day each, the 1890 census, which covered nearly 63 million people, was completed months ahead of schedule and far under budget.
His success did not make the government's problems disappear, however. Hollerith founded his own company in 1896, and for the 1900 census he raised the rent on his machines so sharply that the bureau began building its own. His company joined three others in 1911 and was renamed International Business Machines, or IBM, in 1924. Machines based on his punched cards stayed in use at the bureau until electronic computers replaced them in the 1950s.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: How a train ticket gave an engineer the idea for a new kind of card.
options.B: How an urgent counting problem was solved, and what followed from the solution.
options.C: Why the census office stopped trusting private inventors after 1900.
options.D: How IBM grew from a small company into a maker of electronic computers.

questions.stem: Which of the following questions is answered in the passage?

options.A: How long did it take to finish counting the 1890 census?
options.B: How much did Hollerith charge to rent his machines for the 1900 census?
options.C: How many cards could Hollerith's reader handle in a minute?
options.D: Where did the figures used in the 1888 contest come from?

questions.stem: Suppose a clerk punched the hole for “female” instead of the one for “male” on a man’s card. What would most likely happen when the card was read?

options.A: One more woman would be added to the count.
options.B: The reader would reject the card because no circuit could be completed.
options.C: The man would be counted twice, once in each group.
options.D: The clerk would notice the mistake because no dial would move.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that Hollerith raised the rent on his machines?

options.A: To explain why his company later joined three other firms.
options.B: To suggest that his machines were not really worth their price.
options.C: To show that relying on one inventor brought the government a fresh difficulty.
options.D: To show that the bureau went back to counting by hand after 1900.

translation_zh.text:
美國每十年必須清點全國人口，因為結果決定了各州在國會分得多少席次。到了 1880 年代，這項任務變成一場政府快要輸掉的賽跑。即使有簡單計數機器的幫忙，職員直到 1887 年才把 1880 年的數字加總完畢，距離普查開始已過了大約七年。由於人口持續成長，專家警告 1890 年的普查可能要花 13 年才能處理完，結果會趕不上 1900 年的下一次普查。
赫曼‧何樂禮（Herman Hollerith）是一位曾參與 1880 年普查的年輕工程師，他相信機器能完成這份工作。他的靈感部分來自看到火車查票員在乘客的車票上打洞。他起初試用長條紙卷，後來改用卡片，因為卡片比較耐用，也比較容易送進機器。在他的系統裡，每個人變成一張紙卡，卡上特定位置的一個孔代表一項資料，例如男性、女性或某個年齡。職員把卡片壓進讀卡機時，金屬針會穿過孔，浸入裝著水銀的小杯子。每根穿過去的針都會接通一個電路，讓對應的計數盤往前跳一格。
1888 年，普查辦公室用聖路易市四個地區的舊數字舉辦了一場比賽。兩種對手的方法分別需要 44.5 和 55.5 小時，才能把資料準備好以供計數，何樂禮的方法只要 5.5 小時。他贏得了合約；在每位職員每天打孔約 500 張卡片的情況下，涵蓋將近 6,300 萬人的 1890 年普查比預定提早好幾個月完成，花費也遠低於預算。
然而，他的成功並沒有讓政府的問題就此消失。何樂禮在 1896 年創立了自己的公司，並在 1900 年普查時把機器的租金調漲得非常兇，使普查局開始自己製造機器。他的公司在 1911 年與另外三家公司合併，1924 年改名為國際商業機器公司，也就是 IBM。以他的打孔卡為基礎的機器一直在普查局使用，直到 1950 年代才被電子電腦取代。

open_tasks.prompt: Hollerith's machines saved the census office time and money, but his later rent increase caused new trouble. In 1–2 English sentences, suggest one lesson a government could learn from this story when it buys new technology.
reference_answers: A government should not depend on a single company for an important tool, because that company can raise its prices once the government has no other choice.
When buying new technology, a government should plan how to keep control of it, for example by learning to build or repair the machines itself.
